scenes.title: Healthy graduate pseudopatient writing calmly in a spiral notebook in the hospital dayroom while a nurse charts 'engages in writing behavior'
scenes.era: 1972-1973, American psychiatric ward dayroom & glass nurses' station

layout.description: Brightly lit early-1970s hospital dayroom separated by a wide clear glass partition from the central nurses' charting station; wooden dayroom chairs, a wall clock near 11:55 a.m. outside the dining door, and metal medical chart binders.

positions.who: Pseudopatient Bill Underwood (mannequin in ordinary sweater and jeans)
positions.where: seated calmly in a dayroom chair writing neat field observations openly in a spiral notebook

positions.who: Ward Nurse (mannequin in crisp 1972 white nursing uniform behind glass)
positions.where: glancing once at the notebook and writing 'Patient engages in writing behavior' into an aluminum chart binder
leaning over toward the pseudopatient pointing knowingly at the spiral notebook

props.name: open spiral field notebook
props.period_detail: ordinary college-ruled notebook filled with calm timestamped notes
props.physical_behavior: reinterpreted on the official chart as pathological 'writing behavior'

props.name: aluminum medical chart stamped 'IN REMISSION'
props.period_detail: 1970s metal clipboard showing intake words 'empty, hollow, thud' and discharge stamp 'Schizophrenia in Remission'

props.name: glass-enclosed central nurses' station
props.period_detail: bright partition separating quick 6-minute daily staff contact from dayroom life
props.physical_behavior: illustrates distance between chart label and person

actions.verb_sequence: writes calm timestamped notes openly in his spiral notebook -> Fellow ward patient leans in and gestures 'you're a professor checking up!'
glances through the window -> writes 'engages in writing behavior' onto the aluminum chart

reactions.reaction: looks in quiet disbelief at how plain note-taking gets filtered through the intake label
snaps the aluminum chart shut without asking a single question

scenes.wardrobe: Early-1970s casual sweater and denim on pseudopatient; crisp white 1972 clinical coat/uniform on staff.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1970s institutional daylight — bright, clear documentary framing.
scenes.recognition_hook: Jotting calm field notes in a spiral notebook in full view, a healthy graduate student gets charted behind glass as 'engaging in pathological writing behavior.'

key_visual.description: a calm 1970s graduate student writing in a spiral notebook in a bright hospital dayroom while a nurse behind a glass station writes into an aluminum medical chart

scenes.title: Study 2 reverse challenge: 41 false 'impostor' flags when zero were sent

layout.description: Bright hospital admissions desk with a tally sheet labeled 'Suspected Rosenhan Impostor Rating (1-10)' beside a telephone.

positions.where: circling 'High Confidence Fake' on 41 intake forms

props.name: 41 flagged intake forms vs '0 Sent' folder
props.physical_behavior: proves expectancy swings judgment both ways

actions.verb_sequence: flags 41 incoming forms -> Rosenhan reveals zero pseudopatients were ever dispatched

reactions.reaction: stares stunned at the empty dispatch count

scenes.wardrobe: 1973 white clinical coat and tweed jacket.
scenes.recognition_hook: Warned that impostors were coming, staff flagged 41 patients as fakes — when Rosenhan sent zero.

scenes.title: 1980 DSM-III operational criteria & 2019 archival sleuthing
scenes.era: 2019, archival desk with 1973 folder & DSM-III volume

layout.description: Sunlit research desk holding Bill Underwood's verified 9-day discharge papers, Harry Lando's omitted folder, and the structured 1980 DSM-III manual.

positions.where: comparing verified pseudopatient folders beside omitted records

props.name: verified vs omitted archival folders & DSM-III
props.physical_behavior: shows how science self-corrects both psychiatry and famous papers

actions.verb_sequence: places the verified 'writing behavior' chart next to the omitted ninth folder

reactions.reaction: documents both diagnostic stickiness AND the need for raw data transparency

scenes.recognition_hook: Archival sleuthing confirmed 'writing behavior' really happened — while catching Rosenhan omitting inconvenient files.

scenes.title: Blinding prior reputation labels during a modern work review

layout.description: Clean sunlit desk where a manager reviews anonymized work samples BEFORE opening last year's feedback file.

positions.where: scoring anonymous work deliverables first while past-label folders sit closed to the side

actions.verb_sequence: scores current performance objectively -> only then opens the background file

reactions.reaction: spots strong improvement a sticky old label would have hidden

scenes.recognition_hook: Read today's actual behavior BEFORE opening yesterday's sticky label.
